question: Which key combination is commonly used in Windows OS to open the Task Manager?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ctrl + Shift + Esc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Task Manager** in Windows is a system monitor program used to provide information about the computer's performance and running software. It is also used to end processes and monitor system resources.
 
• The **Ctrl + Shift + Esc** shortcut is the quickest and most direct way to open the Task Manager in Windows. This combination directly launches Task Manager without any intermediary steps. *Hence, this is the correct option.*
 
• Other shortcuts like **Alt + Tab** allow users to switch between open programs and windows but do not open the Task Manager. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• The shortcut **Alt + F4** closes the active window or program but does not access the Task Manager. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• The **Ctrl + Tab** shortcut is used to switch between tabs in a browser or document but does not open the Task Manager. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• The Task Manager can also be accessed using the **Ctrl + Alt + Del** combination, which opens a menu with several options, including Task Manager. However, this combination involves an extra step and is not as direct as Ctrl + Shift + Esc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Features of Task Manager:**

 
 
• The Task Manager provides insights into **CPU usage**, **memory usage**, **disk activity**, and **network usage**. It helps in diagnosing performance issues on a computer.
 
• Users can view and terminate **running processes** or applications that are unresponsive. This is essential for troubleshooting software issues.
 
• The Task Manager also allows users to manage **startup programs**, enabling them to improve the boot time of their system.
 
 
 
• **Methods to Access Task Manager:**
 
 
• Using **Ctrl + Shift + Esc** is the fastest method.
 
• Right-clicking on the **Taskbar** and selecting "Task Manager" is another common way to access it.
 
• Pressing **Ctrl + Alt + Del** and selecting "Task Manager" from the menu is an additional method.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Alt + Tab:** This shortcut is used to switch between open applications but does not open the Task Manager.
 
• **Alt + F4:** This shortcut is used to close the currently active window or program.
 
• **Ctrl + Shift + Esc:** This is the most direct shortcut to access the Task Manager without any intermediate steps.
 
• **Ctrl + Tab:** This is used to navigate between tabs in a browser or document, and it does not open the Task Manager.
 
• **Alternative Access:** Task Manager can also be opened by searching for it in the Start menu or using the Run command (Win + R) and typing **taskmgr**.
